reviewType: AI-assisted factual source review; not clinical approval
editorialAuthorisation: Matt O'Brien authorised evidence-backed informational Watch updates; this is editorial authority, not clinical approval.
scope: Fourteen configured sources reached the seven-day factual-review deadline in two waves on 6 October. Each exact primary document was retrieved in full and read. Every normalized claim fingerprint matched its approved baseline, no withdrawal was detected and no catalogue wording, medicine review date, access statement, supply statement or programme count changed.

unchangedSeparateFailure.disposition: Retained explicitly; this source was not reviewed or greened by the renewal.

fingerprintMethod: Unmodified medicines-watch/monitor.mjs fingerprintSource on complete HTTP 200 responses from each exact checkUrl. Source identity terms were validated before comparison. Response hashes record retrieval evidence; reviewed fingerprints cover normalized claim content.

followUpObservation.disposition: Failures retained explicitly and not greened by the six source renewals.

discoveryPass.scope: Separate current-date and broader undated topic searches covering obesity and weight-management medicines, peptides, oral candidates, combinations, muscle preservation, specialist indications and early, late, paused or discontinued programmes. discoveryPass.limitations: Search indexing is delayed and incomplete, and several results were secondary media summaries. Secondary summaries were not used to renew evidence or add claims. This pass does not establish industry completeness and later primary publications can still require separate review.

sources.assessment: NICE TA664 remains published and continues to recommend liraglutide only for its defined adult subgroup, alongside diet and physical activity and under the guidance conditions. The existing Watch wording still separates the broader licence, the narrower NICE criteria and unverified current supply.

NICE TA494 still does not recommend naltrexone–bupropion within its marketing authorisation for adult weight management and retains the continuation provision for earlier NHS treatment. The existing Watch wording remains accurate and does not infer present stock or private availability.

NICE HST21 still recommends setmelanotide under its conditions for obesity and hunger caused by POMC/PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency in people aged 6 years and over. It does not establish access for every current licensed indication, including acquired hypothalamic obesity.

NICE HST31 still covers genetically confirmed Bardet–Biedl syndrome when treatment starts between ages 6 and 17, with adult continuation until stopping is needed and the commercial arrangement applies. It is not general-obesity access evidence.

Novo Nordisk's dated annual-report narrative still describes cagrilintide separately from CagriSema and describes zenagamtide as a GLP-1/amylin programme in Phase 3 development. It remains sponsor evidence, not proof of UK authorisation, NHS access, supply or equivalent stages across formulations.

Amgen's Q2 update still describes ongoing MARITIME Phase 3 studies and says future AMG 513 development will be discontinued while the existing Phase 1 study follows enrolled participants. Later registry lifecycle additions remain separate and none of this establishes results, approval, NHS access or supply.

Structure's 8 September statement still reports the ACCOMPLISH Phase 3 programme for aleniglipron and early Phase 1/2a ACCG-2671 work. Sponsor-reported measurements and planned readouts are not prescribing claims, clinical approval, UK authorisation, NHS access or supply.

NICE ID6516 remains in development and in progress, with a provisional 10 November 2026 committee meeting and expected publication on 27 January 2027. The existing Watch correctly says NHS access is not confirmed; an appraisal in development is not a funding recommendation or supply evidence.

Novo's complete 21 September statement still reports Phase 3 REIMAGINE 5 and REDEFINE 9 topline results and calls CagriSema investigational. The existing Watch remains bounded to sponsor-reported research and does not infer UK authorisation, NHS access, actual supply or clinical approval.

Viking's complete 29 July update still says injectable VANQUISH-1 and VANQUISH-2 are fully enrolled while oral Phase 3 initiation was expected in the fourth quarter. The Watch continues to distinguish completed enrolment from the planned oral event and infers no UK authorisation, NHS access or supply.

Roche's complete 1 June statement still describes investigational enicepatide Phase 2 findings and movement into Phase 3 development. The existing summary and separately reviewed April presentation remain appropriate; no result, UK authorisation, NHS access, supply or clinical approval is inferred.

The complete Saxenda UK product information still supports the adult BMI and comorbidity criteria, daily administration, gastrointestinal cautions and the 12-week adult response stopping rule. NICE access remains separately sourced and actual supply is not inferred.

The complete Mysimba UK product information still supports the adult BMI and comorbidity criteria, contraindication and interaction cautions, and the 16-week response stopping rule. NICE non-recommendation remains separately sourced and actual supply is not inferred.

The complete Imcivree UK product information still separates acquired hypothalamic obesity from genetically confirmed BBS, POMC/PCSK1 and LEPR indications, including the distinct age thresholds and specialist-prescribing requirement. NICE access remains narrower and separately sourced; actual supply is not inferred.
